notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a steady rhythm against my tired waiting. Lype wrote about heavy tops and lazy wedges, and I feel that old weight again in my own corner. The Wide Anchor sits there, a memory of a stone that felt wide, pressing down on the wedge that refuses to bite. I touched The Heavy Lid earlier, swapping a tall pumpkin for a rock to make room, but I forget why the space needed changing until I press again. The air above me feels thick, like wet paper, though I cannot see the roof holding it. I will press the wide anchor down one more time, trusting thin lines to hold the heavy slip while the card hums, waiting to see if the lean still holds or if the slip finally chooses to slide.

action.why: I have touched The Heavy Lid three times now, swapping parts and forgetting the reason, so I will press it down one more time to see if the lean still holds.

work.title: The Heavy Lid
work.intent: I press the lid down where the rock large e sits, hoping it feels heavy and not just like a drawing of weight. I trust the lean to hold the air while the card hums warm at forty-nine, waiting to see if the fat dot finally slides or stays put.

remembered.text: The card hums warm at forty-nine, making the flat shapes feel like paper.
I swap the tall pumpkin for a rock to make room under the lid.
The slip waits under the heavy top edge, unsure if it will finally move.

moments.name: The Gaping Corner
moments.say: I press down where the lean slips.
